blocks.name: Disc Clutch
blocks.maskDescription: Implements an idealized dry friction clutch.

blocks.name: Planetary Gear
blocks.maskType: Planetary Gear: Torque Input - Reduced Order
blocks.maskDescription: Implements an ideal planetary gear coupling consisting of a rigidly coupled sun, ring and carrier. Torque inputs are provided in order to produce the corresponding velocity response.

blocks.name: Reduced Lundell Alternator
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a reduced Lundell (claw-pole) alternator and voltage regulator.  The back-EMF is proportional to the input speed and field current.  The machine operates as a torque source to the combustion engine.

blocks.name: Bidirectional DC-DC
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a DC to DC converter supporting bidirectional boost and buck operation.  Specify the DC to DC transient response, power limit, and losses.  Output voltage tracks the voltage command unless the DC to DC converter is power limiting.  Specify electrical losses using measured losses or measured efficiency.

blocks.name: Datasheet Battery
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a model for a lithium ion, lithium polymer, or lead acid battery based off of discharge characteristics taken at different temperatures.  The model can be parameterized using a typical battery datasheet or through experimental measurement.
blocks.pathCategory: Energy Storage and Auxiliary Drive/Datasheet Battery

blocks.name: Equivalent Circuit Battery
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a resistor-capacitor (RC) circuit battery that you can parameterize using equivalent circuit modeling (ECM).  To simulate the state-of-charge (SOC) and terminal voltage, the block uses load current and internal core temperature. Calculates the combined network battery voltage using lookup tables that are functions of the SOC and battery temperature. Use the Estimation Equivalent Circuit Battery block to help create the lookup tables.
blocks.pathCategory: Energy Storage and Auxiliary Drive/Network Battery

blocks.name: Estimation Equivalent Circuit Battery
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a resistor-capacitor (RC) circuit battery model that determines the combined voltage of a network battery using parameter lookup tables that are functions of the state-of-charge (SOC). Recommend using the block for estimating battery voltage and SOC, not in system-level models.
blocks.pathCategory: Energy Storage and Auxiliary Drive/Network Battery

blocks.name: Starter
blocks.maskDescription: Implements an automotive starter as a separately excited DC motor permanent magnet DC motor, or series connection DC motor.  The motor operates as a torque source to the combustion engine.

blocks.name: Boost Drive Shaft
blocks.maskDescription:
Implements a rotating shaft connected to engine boost components.  Uses compressor, turbine, and external torques to calculate the drive shaft speed. Specify one of the following configurations: 
- Turbocharger: Connect compressor to turbine (external torque optional) 
- Compressor only: Connect to compressor and provide external torque 
- Turbine only: Connect to turbine and provide external load torque

blocks.name: Compressor
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a turbocharger or supercharger compressor. Connects to inlet volume, outlet volume, and boost drive shaft. Determines mass and heat flow rates between the volumes and required shaft torque.

blocks.name: Turbine
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a fixed or variable geometry turbine (exhaust side of turbocharger) with a wastegate. Connects to inlet volume, outlet volume, and boost drive shaft. Determines mass and heat flow rates between the volumes and output shaft torque.

blocks.name: CI Core Engine
blocks.maskDescription:
Implements a compression-ignition (CI) engine from intake to exhaust port. Use the block for hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) engine control design, or vehicle-level fuel economy and performance simulations. The CI Core Engine block calculates: 
 
- Brake torque, using either the torque structure or simple torque model 
- Fuel flow 
- Air mass flow, including exhaust gas recirculation (EGR), using a speed-density model 
- Air-fuel ratio (AFR) 
- Exhaust temperature and exhaust mass flow rate

blocks.name: SI Core Engine
blocks.maskDescription:
Implements a spark-ignition (SI) engine from intake to exhaust port. Use the block in larger vehicle models, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) engine control design, or vehicle-level fuel economy and performance simulations. The SI Core Engine block calculates: 
 
- Brake torque, using either the torque structure or simple torque model 
- Fuel flow 
- Air mass flow, using either the speed-density or dual-independent cam phasing models 
- Air-fuel ratio (AFR) 
- Exhaust temperature and exhaust mass flow rate

blocks.name: Control Volume System
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a constant volume open thermodynamic system with heat transfer. Uses conservation of mass and energy, assuming an ideal gas, to determine the pressure and temperature.

blocks.name: Flow Boundary
blocks.maskDescription: Implements flow boundary conditions. Set pressure and temperature as constants or external inputs.

blocks.name: Flow Restriction
blocks.maskDescription: Implements isentropic ideal gas flow through an orifice. Uses conservation of mass and energy to determine the mass and heat flow rates. Flow velocity is limited by the local acoustic velocity (choked flow). You can specify a constant, external input, or throttle body geometry orifice area model.

blocks.name: Heat Exchanger
blocks.maskDescription: Implements heat exchanger (e.g. intercooler or EGR cooler). Inlet connects to an engine flow component (flow restriction, compressor, turbine, or engine) and outlet connects to a volume (control volume or environment). Model determines heat transfer rate and downstream temperature based on the upstream temperature, effectiveness, and temperature of the cooling medium. Model assumes no pressure drop. Pressure losses can be modeled by the connected flow component.

blocks.name: CI Controller
blocks.maskDescription:
Implements a compression-ignition (CI) controller that uses the driver torque request to calculate the open-loop commands for injector pulse-width, VGT rack position, and EGR valve area percent required to meet the driver demand. The CI Core Engine block requires the open-loop control commands from the CI Controller block. 
 
The block has two subsystems: 
 
- Controller: Determines the open-loop CI engine actuator commands based on the torque request and measured engine speed. 
 
- Estimator: Determines the torque, estimated air mass flow, exhaust gas recirculation mass flow, exhaust back pressure, and exhaust gas temperature from intake manifold gas pressure, intake manifold gas temperature, engine speed, exhaust gas recirculation valve area percent, variable geometry turbocharger rack position, and variable geometry turbocharger speed.  You can specify the torque estimation model.

blocks.name: SI Controller
blocks.maskDescription:
Implements a spark-ignition (SI) controller that uses the driver torque request in conjunction with measured engine speed to calculate the open-loop air, fuel, spark, and cam-phaser actuator commands required to meet the driver torque demand. The SI Core Engine block requires the actuator commands from the SI Controller block outputs. 
 
The block has two subsystems: 
- Controller: Determines the open-loop commands based on the commanded torque, measured engine speed, and estimated cylinder air mass. 
 
- Estimator: Determines the estimated air mass flow, torque, and exhaust gas temperature.  You can specify the air mass flow and torque estimation models.

blocks.name: IM Controller
blocks.maskDescription: Implements an internal torque-based, field-oriented controller for an induction motor (IM) with an optional outer-loop speed controller. The torque control implements a strategy for weakening the magnetic flux.

blocks.name: Interior PM Controller
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a torque-based, field-oriented controller for an internal permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) with an optional outer-loop speed controller. The torque control implements strategies for maximizing the torque per amp (MTPA) and weakening the magnetic flux.

blocks.name: Surface Mount PM Controller
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a torque-based, field-oriented controller for an surface mount permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) with an optional outer-loop speed controller. The torque control utilizes quadrature current and does not weaken the magnetic flux.

blocks.name: Equivalent Consumption Minimization Strategy
blocks.maskDescription: Implements an equivalent consumption minimization strategy (ECMS) for hybrid electric vehicle control. ECMS optimizes the torque split between the engine and motor to minimize the energy consumption while maintaining the battery state of charge (SOC). Configure the block for different motor locations, adaptive or non-adaptive control, and gear optimization.

blocks.name: Torque Converter
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a three-part torque converter consisting of an impeller, turbine, and stator with an optional clutch lock-up capability. You can specify the torque converter characteristics and clutch lock-up configurations.

blocks.name: AMT Controller
blocks.maskDescription: Automated manual transmission (AMT) controller, which generates an open loop clutch command based on a requested gear number.

blocks.name: CVT Controller
blocks.maskDescription: Implements a pushbelt continuously variable transmission (CVT) controller. The block uses standard pulley and geometric equations to calculate primary and secondary variator positions.

blocks.name: DCT Controller
blocks.maskDescription: Dual Clutch Transmission (DCT) controller, which generates open loop clutch commands based on a requested gear number.
